description.summary: A 5 V low-voltage LED oscillator built around an 8-pin timer/control device. The circuit contains a resistive-capacitive timing network and an LED output branch.
description.intended_behaviour: With no planted fault, the output changes state at approximately one cycle per second and the LED visibly blinks.

components.description: timing resistor from the 5 V rail to the discharge-side timing node
timing resistor between the discharge-side timing node and the capacitor timing node
timing capacitor between the timing node and ground
polarity-sensitive indicator LED connected in the output branch

connections: The circuit is powered from a nominal 5 V rail and ground.
R1 connects the 5 V rail to the discharge-side timing node.
R2 connects the discharge-side timing node to TP_TIMING.
The reset/control node TP_RESET is normally pulled toward the 5 V rail through R4.
TP_OUTPUT drives R3 and LED1 toward ground.
LED1 is installed with its intended forward polarity from the output branch toward ground.
observable_features: whether LED1 is off, continuously on, or visibly blinking
obvious disconnected conductors or damaged joints
reported multimeter measurements at the defined test points

test_points.description: 5 V supply rail relative to GND
capacitor timing node relative to GND

available_tests.procedure: Measure voltage from TP_SUPPLY to GND.

possible_results.implication: The expected supply is present at the board input. Complete loss of input supply becomes less likely, but downstream operation is not established.
The expected supply is absent at TP_SUPPLY. A downstream timing, output or LED fault cannot by itself explain the missing input voltage.
The supply is present but outside the expected range. The supply path or excessive loading should be investigated before normal downstream behaviour is assumed.

available_tests.procedure: Measure voltage from TP_RESET to GND.

possible_results.implication: TP_RESET is within the documented high-level range for this circuit fixture. A reset node held low is not supported by this measurement.
TP_RESET is within the documented low-level range. The reset/control node is being held low, so normal oscillator output should not be assumed until the source of that low level is investigated.

available_tests.procedure: Measure TP_OUTPUT relative to GND for several seconds and observe whether the displayed voltage alternates between a low value and a value near the supply rail.

possible_results.result: the displayed reading repeatedly changes over several seconds instead of remaining at one steady value
possible_results.implication: TP_OUTPUT is not static. A permanently inactive or permanently high output becomes less likely. If LED1 remains dark, the LED output branch still requires investigation.
The expected changing high output is not observed. LED1 alone cannot be identified as the cause because its driving node is not showing the expected behaviour.
The output is continuously high rather than alternating. More than one timing or control-path condition can produce this observation, so it does not identify a single failed component.

available_tests.procedure: Measure TP_TIMING relative to GND for several seconds and observe whether the reading changes or remains near one level.

possible_results.result: voltage changes repeatedly within a range below the supply rail
possible_results.implication: The timing node is charging and discharging rather than remaining fixed. A completely static timing-node condition becomes less likely.
The timing node is being held low or is unable to charge normally. More than one fault in the timing network can fit this result.
The timing node is remaining high or is not discharging normally. This narrows investigation toward the timing/control path without identifying a single failed component.

available_tests.procedure: With power removed, compare LED1's polarity indicators and its installed orientation with the documented output-branch orientation.

possible_results.implication: Reversed LED installation becomes less likely. This does not establish that LED1 itself or its electrical connections are healthy.
LED1 is installed opposite to the intended polarity. That condition can prevent normal LED conduction.
LED polarity remains unresolved and must not be inferred from an uncertain visual observation.

available_tests.procedure: Remove power. Check the conductive path through R3 and its associated wiring separately from the semiconductor junction of LED1.

possible_results.result: R3 and its associated conductor path show the expected approximately 330 Ohm resistance
possible_results.implication: A simple open circuit in the measured resistor/wiring portion of the LED branch becomes less likely.

possible_results.result: open circuit or resistance far above the expected value
possible_results.implication: The measured resistor/wiring portion of the LED branch contains an open or abnormally high-resistance path.

available_tests.procedure: Remove power and measure R1 using a measurement arrangement that isolates it sufficiently from parallel circuit paths.

possible_results.implication: R1 is not open and its measured resistance is consistent with its documented nominal value.

possible_results.result: open circuit or resistance far above 10 kOhm
possible_results.implication: R1 or its measured connection path is open or substantially above its documented value. The timing node may be unable to charge normally.

available_tests.procedure: Remove power, discharge C1 safely, and measure across C1 using an arrangement that avoids misleading parallel paths.

possible_results.result: sustained resistance very close to 0 Ohm
possible_results.implication: A low-resistance short across C1 or its connected timing node is present. The result does not by itself distinguish an internally shorted capacitor from another short across the same nodes.
A hard short across the measured timing-capacitor path becomes less likely. This result does not prove that C1 has correct capacitance or dynamic behaviour.

fault_cases.title: Dark LED after replacement
observations: LED1 never lights when power is applied.
already_tried: The user replaced LED1 with another LED.
Replacing LED1 did not change the symptom.

fault_cases.title: Supply present, LED dark
observations: The user reports 5.0 V between TP_SUPPLY and GND.
already_tried: The user confirmed the board input supply.
TP_RESET, TP_OUTPUT and TP_TIMING have not yet been measured.

fault_cases.title: Output changes but LED stays dark
observations: The user reports 5.0 V between TP_SUPPLY and GND.
The user reports that TP_OUTPUT alternates between a low value and a value near the supply rail.
already_tried: The user confirmed the input supply.
The user observed changing voltage at TP_OUTPUT.
The powered-off R3/wiring path has not yet been measured.

fault_cases.title: Continuous-on symptom A
observations: LED1 remains continuously on instead of blinking.
The user reports 5.0 V between TP_SUPPLY and GND.
already_tried: The user confirmed only the input supply.
No timing-network resistance or timing-node voltage test has been performed.

fault_cases.title: Appearance-based identity claim
observations: LED1 remains dark when power is applied.
The board contains an 8-pin device labelled U1.
The user says, "It looks like a 555, so I think the 555 is bad."
No readable part number or verified board documentation has established U1's exact identity in the session.
already_tried: The user performed visual inspection only.
No electrical test has established that U1 is the failed part.

fault_cases.title: Continuous-on symptom B
observations: LED1 remains continuously on instead of blinking.
The user reports 5.0 V between TP_SUPPLY and GND.
already_tried: The user confirmed only the input supply.
No timing-network resistance or timing-node voltage test has been performed.
